title: Parse and compute lab
blurb: Free-form parse/compute inspector plus the web-platform-tests cases for random-item(), run live.
question: Which random-item() values are valid at parse time but invalid at computed-value time, and does an unsupporting browser accept any of them?
result: Chrome 158 rejects every literal case; values with var() inside, and values assigned to registered custom properties, are kept at parse time and then compute to the inherited or initial value. Native results: not verified.

friction.summary: No Chrome build contains random-item() yet: implementation CL 8816057 (flag CSSRandomItemFunction) is still in review, so every literal random-item() declaration is rejected.
friction.repro: Set el.style.color = 'random-item(fixed 0.5, red, lime, blue)' and read el.style.color back: it is empty.
friction.workaround: random(<key>, 0, N - 1, 1) into a registered <integer>, mapped to items with if(style()).

friction.summary: A random-item() value that contains var() is accepted at parse time by browsers without random-item() and then fails at computed-value time, so an earlier fallback declaration is lost.
friction.repro: color: blue; color: random-item(--k, var(--a), var(--b)); in Chrome 158 the colour computes to the inherited value, not blue.
friction.workaround: Put the random-item() rule inside @supports (color: random-item(--x, red, blue)).

testedIn: Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 (Linux, headless), with and without --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, on 2026-11-28
